package_info.package_versions: Unknown (impacts over 40,000 users as of report date)
package_info.why_malicious: The plugin contains two critical vulnerabilities: a privilege-escalation flaw and a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) bug, both of which can be exploited to inject and execute malicious code on vulnerable websites, allowing attackers to escalate privileges or run arbitrary scripts.

execution_context.file_location: WordPress plugin PHP files (Orbit Fox core code)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks for a 'role' parameter in POST requests and sets the current user's role to the provided value without proper authorization checks, enabling privilege escalation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing any user to set their own role via a POST parameter is highly suspicious and dangerous, as it enables privilege escalation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal plugin behavior should restrict role changes to authorized administrators and validate permissions before making such changes. This code allows arbitrary role changes by any authenticated user.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate role changes should only occur in admin panels with nonce and capability checks.
key_indicators: Direct use of user-supplied input to set user roles
Lack of capability or nonce checks

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user input processed and displayed on site)
execution_context.file_location: WordPress plugin PHP files (Orbit Fox core code)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code stores user-supplied input from a POST parameter directly into a WordPress option and later outputs it to the page without sanitization, enabling stored XSS.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Storing and displaying user input without sanitization or escaping allows attackers to inject malicious JavaScript, leading to stored XSS.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal plugin behavior should sanitize and escape all user-supplied content before storing or displaying it.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate plugins may store user content, but must always sanitize and escape it.
key_indicators: Direct storage and output of unsanitized user input
No use of esc_html(), esc_attr(), or similar WordPress functions

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends crafted POST request to escalate privileges by setting their user role to administrator.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains admin access to the WordPress site.

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious JavaScript payload into the 'custom_text' field via POST request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious script is stored in the database and executed in the browser of any user visiting the affected page (stored XSS).

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected user role changes via POST requests from non-admin users
User-supplied content stored and rendered without sanitization (leading to XSS)
file_indicators: PHP files in Orbit Fox plugin handling user roles or storing/displaying user input without sanitization
network_indicators: POST requests to WordPress endpoints with 'role' or 'custom_text' parameters from untrusted sources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for POST requests to WordPress endpoints that attempt to change user roles or submit custom text fields, especially from non-administrator users. Audit plugin code for direct use of user input in role assignment or output to pages without sanitization. Use web application firewalls to detect and block suspicious payloads indicative of XSS or privilege escalation attempts.
